## Summary

Describe the change, which checkpoint/authority it uses, and whether it changes reader-facing data or only project instructions.

## Publication boundary — mandatory for public-facing changes

- [ ] I read project/PUBLICATION_STANDARD.md and project/PUBLIC_COPY_REMEDIATION.md.
- [ ] No original research wording, audit notes, source-access/tool commentary, internal IDs or private fields are delivered in public HTML/JS/JSON, not merely hidden from sight.
- [ ] Claims, dates and alternative explanations retain their verified source support and meaningful uncertainty; no uninspected source is represented as verified.
- [ ] Public source references remain accessible and useful. Young Explorers retains its own appropriate adaptation.
- [ ] Both editions and all affected municipality fields have been reviewed; for a statewide copy-release, all 564 per edition have documented outcomes.
- [ ] Existing C21/C57/Review27 identities, asset baselines, category guards and notebook behavior are unchanged or separately approved with exact before/after evidence.
- [ ] Automated scan results are reviewed as **candidates**, not as proof of editorial approval. Any remaining exposure is documented and blocks copy-release sign-off.
- [ ] I checked the rendered site, delivered payloads, keyboard/mobile behavior and live URL after deployment, or explicitly marked these as pending.

For a **policy/docs-only** PR, check only applicable items and state that the live Atlas remains uncleared if its known copy issues are not corrected.
